meta.description: Test read. A transient message bar with an optional leading icon, trailing action and description. Read independently of the existing Toast page, and the first test to resolve every binding through the token database.

verdict.title: Restructure — the axes do not describe independent choices
verdict.text: Tokens hold: 500 fields resolve, none drift. But the six axes allow 96 and build 22, Theme does nothing to Destructive, Pending differs from Default only by icon, and MD and SM are built as two different components.

overview.inContextNote: A short confirmation that floats above the bottom of a screen after an action — a transfer sent, a setting saved — and clears itself. Sketched; no screenshot of a shipping screen was read in this pass.
overview.inContextAlt: A mobile screen with a dark Toast near the bottom, a check icon and a one-line confirmation message.

traits.name: Reusable
traits.note: Any short confirmation, error or progress message. The message, description and action are content, and the text and action are slots — nothing is tied to one product.

traits.name: Self-contained
traits.note: Owns its surface, layout and icon placement; the action is a DS Button - XSmall instance and the description a Subtext Message instance.

traits.name: Consistent
traits.note: The same toast is built several ways. MD wraps the icon in a LeadingIcon frame, SM does not; the surface, border and radius sit on ToastRow in plain variants and on the root in action variants; the title layer is named Title, #content or LeadingIcon; the shadow exists on 8 of 22 variants; and the icon colour is bound to three different tokens from three different families.

traits.name: Composable
traits.note: The action is a Button instance set to the right appearance per tone — a pill on Dark and Light, a text link on Destructive — and the text and action areas are real Slots.

behavior.notes: Neutral confirmation with a check icon. Dark: #0A2757 surface; Light: #FFFFFF surface with a #E5EBF4 border.
Red #D61B2C surface with a circled-✕ icon — under both Theme values. Its action is a text-link Retry, not a pill.
Identical to Default except the icon, which is the information glyph. Only built with the icon on.
Same 312 × 38 box. Title drops from 14 to 12 (Primary/Multi-line Label/Light/Fine), icon from 24 to 16 and centres, and the shadow is gone. Never built with an action or description.
Row becomes 41 tall, title turns bold (Primary/Multi-line Label/Small) and a 24-tall Button sits on the right. Never built with a leading icon.
No close control and no timing is specified — nothing on the component says how long it stays or how it leaves.

open.headline: Appearance and Theme are not independent.
open.body: Destructive draws red under both Theme values: its four plain variants all sit under Theme=Dark and its two action variants all under Theme=Light, split arbitrarily. Pending differs from Default only in the leading icon. The six axes allow 96 combinations; 22 are built.

open.headline: The axes gate each other.
open.body: hasDescription=True exists only with hasTrailingAction=True; Size=SM never has an action or a description; an action never has a leading icon; Pending never lacks one. A consumer cannot turn a property on without knowing which others it silently depends on. All three has… properties are also string variants rather than booleans.

open.headline: MD and SM are built as two different components.
open.body: MD wraps the icon in a LeadingIcon frame with a raw 7 top padding and tops it; SM places the icon straight in ToastRow and centres it. The surface, border and 8 radius sit on ToastRow in plain variants but on the variant root in action variants, with the border CENTER in one and INSIDE in another.

open.headline: The title layer has three names.
open.body: The same text role is Title in most variants, #content in Default · Dark · action, and LeadingIcon — an icon name — in both Destructive action variants. Mapped to code, the name tells a developer the wrong thing.

open.headline: The same values are bound in some variants and typed in others.
open.body: ToastRow padding 12 is space/space-12 in 16 variants and raw in 6; padding 8, gap 24 and radius 8 are likewise raw where siblings bind them. The shadow 0 1 3 0 #E8EEF2 @79% is unbound on all 8 variants that carry it, and LeadingIcon top padding is a raw, off-scale 7.

open.headline: The icon colour is bound to three tokens from three families.
open.body: Default Dark binds border/color-border-primary-inverse, Pending Dark binds bg/color-bg-main, Light binds text/color-text. All draw the right colour today, but a border or background token retuned tomorrow recolours these icons with it.

open.headline: The description fails contrast on two tones.
open.body: At 10px (Secondary/Bold/Small Caption): Destructive #F6F9FD @80% on #D61B2C is 3.54:1; Light #6780A9 on #FFFFFF is 4.01:1. Both under 4.5:1. Dark passes at 7.79:1. Computed from the resolved tokens with the WCAG formula.

open.headline: The icons are unflattened unions carrying dead paint.
open.body: Each leading icon is a BOOLEAN_OPERATION whose child vectors still carry raw #025AE9 strokes — 30 of them. A union draws its own fill, so they never render, but they ship in every variant. Destructive also uses the Close glyph, which reads as a dismiss button.

recommendations.headline: Split tone from theme.
recommendations.body: Make Appearance a tone — Neutral or Destructive — and apply Theme only where it changes something. Destructive then stops occupying two Theme values it ignores.

recommendations.headline: Make the leading icon a slot, not an appearance.
recommendations.body: Pending is Default with a different icon. An icon slot with preferred instances (check, information, error) removes the Pending axis and lets new messages pick an icon without a new variant.

recommendations.headline: Build MD and SM from one structure.
recommendations.body: One frame tree, with Size changing only the title style and icon size. Put the surface, border and radius on one layer in every variant.

recommendations.headline: Bind the shadow and the six raw paddings.
recommendations.body: Give the shadow an elevation token and bind the paddings that siblings already bind. Replace the raw 7 with a spacing token or a centred icon.

recommendations.headline: Bind every icon to one text-family token per tone.
recommendations.body: Use text/color-text-inverse on Dark and Destructive and text/color-text on Light, so icon colour follows text colour and nothing else.

recommendations.headline: Raise the description to 4.5:1, and name the title layer once.
recommendations.body: Lift the Destructive and Light description tokens; rename every title layer to #title so it maps to one parameter.

recommendations.headline: Specify duration and dismissal.
recommendations.body: How long it shows, whether it can be swiped away, and how it is announced to assistive technology — none of it is on the component.

accessibility.ios: Post UIAccessibility.post(notification: .announcement, argument: message) — a toast that is only drawn is never heard.
accessibility.android: Give the container liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Polite (Assertive for Destructive).

accessibility.ios: Extend the timeout while VoiceOver is running, or keep it until dismissed when it carries an action.
accessibility.android: Use SnackbarDuration.Indefinite when there is an action, so it is reachable by TalkBack.

accessibility.ios: Prefix Destructive announcements ("Error: …"); the red surface carries nothing to VoiceOver.
accessibility.android: Put the tone in contentDescription for Destructive.

accessibility.ios: The action is a Button with a 44 pt hit area, not only its 24-tall drawn pill.
Hide the leading icon with .accessibilityHidden(true); the message already says it.
accessibility.android: Set contentDescription = null on the leading icon.

usageGuidelines.doText: Use Toast for a short, non-blocking confirmation of something that just happened.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Do not use it for errors the user must resolve before continuing — that needs an Alert or an inline error.

usageGuidelines.doText: Add an action only when it undoes or retries the thing just done.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Do not put navigation in a toast; it disappears before most users reach it.

usageGuidelines.doText: Keep the message to one line at 312 wide.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Do not rely on the description for anything important; it is 10px and below the contrast minimum on two tones.

scorecard.notes: MD and SM use different frame trees, the surface sits on different layers in plain and action variants, and the title is named Title, #content or LeadingIcon depending on the variant.
22 of 96 combinations built; axes gate each other; Theme is a no-op on Destructive and Pending is an icon preset. The three has… properties are string variants.

Measured through the token database: 500 fields resolve to named tokens with 0 drift and 0 unknown. Against it: an unbound shadow on 8 variants, six paddings raw where siblings bind them, a raw 7, and icon colours bound to border and background tokens.

Maps to one message, an action and an icon, but a native API has to encode which parameters are valid together — Theme ignored on Destructive, description only with an action — or it will render combinations Figma never drew.
The action inherits its states from Button. Nothing specifies duration or dismissal, and the description is 3.54:1 on Destructive and 4.01:1 on Light at 10px.
The icons export cleanly, but each is an unflattened union with 30 raw #025AE9 child strokes that never draw, and the error state uses the Close glyph.

rows.body: Independent trial read of Toast, the first run through the token database. The component already has a page at Toast; this one was written from a fresh read without consulting it. It stays out of the sidebar, search, the grid and the counts.

Every bound field was resolved by scripts/audit/figma-verify.mjs against src/data/tokens.json: 500 token, 0 drift, 0 unknown. Token names on this page come from that lookup, not from matching hex values.

figma-verify reported 2 drift and 30 extra raw values that are not real: it does not multiply paint opacity into a translucent token's alpha, and it counts paints on the children of a boolean operation, which never draw. Both were corrected by hand for this page and reported for the checker.
The existing page gives the breakdown as Default 14, Destructive 6, Pending 4 — 24, against its own total of 22. The set holds Default 12.
